title: Normalized scalar quotient presentation determines the coherent counit by double transpose
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E\subset L/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$, uniformizers $\varpi_E,\varpi_L$ and an embedding $\iota:E\to L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a scheme $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. On $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ put $A_{E,m}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m)_W$, $B_m=(\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^m)_W$ and $R_E=\varprojlim_mA_{E,m}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], with the same-index coefficient maps $A_{E,m}\to B_m$ and actual quotient transitions of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Let $S_Y$ be a normalized primitive scalar realization model for $\iota$ on $W$ in the sense of [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models], let $A$ be an object of the derived category of $R_E$-modules, and let $P\to A$ be a representative by a flat-term K-flat complex $P$ of $R_E$-modules [def-a1-flat-term-kflat-complex]. Let $C(P)$ be the strict $B_\bullet$-system with term $C(P)_m=(P\otimes_{R_E}A_{E,m})\otimes^L_{A_{E,m}}B_m$, let $a_m:C(P)_m\xrightarrow{\sim}P\otimes_{R_E}B_m$ be $(x\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes ab$, and use the actual quotient transitions. The canonical quotient presentation $(P,C(P),e_P,a)$ supplied by the normalized realization/effectivity data satisfies $\operatorname{CoefficientReductionPresentation}(P,C(P),e_P,a)$ of [def-pur-coefficient-reduction-presentation]. Let $u_{S_Y,P}$ be the scalar realization isomorphism and let $e_{C(P)}$ be the coherent reduction/realization counit. After identifying the target by the $a_m$, the composite $c_{S_Y,P}=e_{C(P)}\circ\mathcal R_L(u_{S_Y,P})$ is the unique coherent system morphism whose double transpose under the reduction/total-limit adjunction and the constant-tower/total-limit adjunction is the localization of the strict tensor-unit map determined by the $a_m$. The canonical coherent counit comparison $c^{\mathrm{can}}_P$ of [lem-pur-coefficient-extension-reduction-model] has the same double transpose; hence uniqueness of transposes gives $c_{S_Y,P}=c^{\mathrm{can}}_P$ as an entire coherent quotient-system morphism, with all actual transitions retained. This identifies the arbitrary normalized model comparison with the coefficient-extension model comparison before any finite-level evaluation.

source.place: The scalar-extension comparison is the transpose of scalar-extended evaluation; after the tensor associator the nested composites transpose to the same evaluation, so uniqueness of transposes gives equality.
